title: The sky is falling
hookLine: a hare hears a fruit fall and starts a stampede; a lion checks the facts (Jataka 322)

lines: A FRUIT DROPS ON A LEAF.
cards: Thud. A hare is lying under a palm tree, near a grove of vilva trees, turning over an anxious thought: if the earth broke apart, what would become of me?
Just then a ripe vilva fruit drops onto a dry palm leaf right beside him. Thud. He doesn't look round to see what it was.
He's already running, and shouting as he goes. The old saying has the sky falling. In this Jataka tale, it's the earth.

teach.b: First, the run. The hare cries that the earth is breaking up. Another hare sees him running and runs too, without asking why.
Then more hares, then deer and boars, buffaloes and tigers, even elephants, a whole forest pounding toward the sea.
Second, the lion. A lion sees the stampede and asks the one question nobody has asked: who saw the earth breaking up? The elephants don't know; the tigers told them.
The tigers point to others, and so on down the line, back to the hares, and the hares point at one hare. Third, the check. Where were you when you heard it, the lion asks.
He takes the hare on his back and goes to the spot.
There's the palm leaf, and the fruit lying on it. Fourth, the return.
The lion goes back and tells the herd what he found, and the animals, who were running toward the sea, are saved.

In the tale the lion is the Buddha in an earlier life, and his gift is not strength or speed: one question, and the patience to walk back and look. A frightening thing passes from mouth to mouth and grows as it goes.
Everyone runs because someone else is running. Nobody goes back to the palm leaf.

how: Buddhist teaching on right speech asks whether words are true, helpful and timely before they're spoken, and teachers sometimes use this tale to show how a rumor grows.

o: a message passed from one hare to the next
the small true cause behind a big scare
a sign that the earth is breaking up

games.q: the hare and the lion: tap the pairs.

s: in the Jataka the hare cries that the sky is falling
the hare cries that the earth is breaking up.
the lion carried the hare back to the spot
and there was the palm leaf, with the fruit lying on it.
it began with one hare and spread all the way up to the elephants.

games.q: you're the lion, and the whole forest is stampeding past you toward the sea. what do you do?
o: run with them; they must know something.
ask who saw it, and go back to look.
roar to make them run faster.
games.why: the lion traces the story back to one hare, carries him to the spot, finds the fruit on the palm leaf, and saves the herd.

practice: Let the mind bring up one worry it's picked up from somewhere, passed along, half-heard, shared without a source, and watch how fast it wants to run. Then ask the lion's question: who saw it, and where's the palm leaf?
No answer is needed now; just feel the difference between a thud and a falling world.

wordCard.voice: Palm leaf. What a lion found at the bottom of a rumor, a hare's fruit fallen onto a dry palm leaf, after the whole forest stampeded toward the sea. Today's word.
